subject.title: sessions_spawn from a CLI-harness parent (claude-cli) clamps subagents to gateway bridge tools — children lose exec/read/write

question: Should CLI-harness bridge-visible allowlists be treated as inheritable child restrictions, or should inheritance account for native harness file/shell capabilities that OpenClaw intentionally omits from the MCP bridge?
rationale: This choice controls whether spawned children may retain file/shell tools when the parent harness has them natively; automation should not decide that authorization boundary without owner intent.

options.title: Use Capability-Aware Inheritance
options.body: Treat native CLI-harness file/shell capabilities as part of the parent privilege model while still inheriting real configured/profile/group/sandbox restrictions into children.

options.title: Keep Bridge-Visible Clamp
options.body: Preserve current non-escalation behavior and document that CLI-harness parents spawn children with only the OpenClaw bridge-visible tool set.

options.title: Add An Explicit Operator Knob
options.body: Introduce an opt-in inheritance mode only if maintainers decide this boundary must stay configurable rather than automatic.

recommendation.title: Use Capability-Aware Inheritance
recommendation.body: Treat native CLI-harness file/shell capabilities as part of the parent privilege model while still inheriting real configured/profile/group/sandbox restrictions into children.

likelyOwner.reason: He fixed the closely related claude-cli loopback deny-side boundary in PR 88946 and is the strongest available owner signal for the security tradeoff.
